_comment: Inputs for build_panoramas.py. Each entry is one rover panorama placed at a stop. Positions come from shared/poses/<site>_poses.csv at the nearest sol. hfov_deg is the horizontal span the image covers; center_heading_deg is the compass bearing of the image's centre column (null: use the rover pose heading, which is approximate for a stitched mosaic). walkability and next_orbiter_pass are demo values for the 360-degree view, not measurements. Images not listed here but dropped in data/raw/panos/ as <site>_sol<N>.jpg are picked up with defaults. POI headings: features with a known location (Mount Sharp summit, Bradbury Landing, Jezero's western delta front) use the true bearing from the stop; near-field rocks and hazards are placed below the horizon at an illustrative bearing. Because the image orientation is approximate, a pin can sit a few degrees off the feature in the photo.

pois.title: Western Delta Front
pois.detail: The eroded front of Jezero's ancient river delta, about 2.8 km west. Layered sediments laid down in standing water: the mission's prime astrobiology target.

pois.title: Descent-Stage Scour
pois.detail: Fine dust blown off by the sky crane's engines exposes flat, smooth rock. Low-traction footing when dusted over: shorten your stride.

pois.title: Mount Sharp Summit
pois.detail: Aeolis Mons rises about 5 km above the crater floor, 33 km to the southeast. Its stacked layers record Gale's change from a wet to a dry climate.

pois.title: Angular Float Rocks
pois.detail: Sharp, wind-faceted cobbles like those that punctured Curiosity's aluminium wheels. Step between them, not on them; suit boot soles are the weak point.

pois.title: Gale Crater Floor
pois.detail: Looking north across Aeolis Palus toward Bradbury Landing, about 10 km away, where Curiosity touched down in 2012. Dust haze softens the far rim.

pois.title: Sand-Filled Trough
pois.detail: Soft wind-blown sand pooled between rock ledges. Boots can sink and slip: probe with a pole before committing weight, or route around.
